identity: An Arabic Wikipedia article on قلعة حلب (the Citadel of Aleppo). Encyclopedic factual prose: a two-paragraph lead, then a التاريخ section broken into sub-sections whose headings (التاريخ / السلوقيون / الرومان والبيزنطيون / العصور الإسلامية المبكرة) each sit alone between two <NL> tokens. Register is neutral third-person historical narration built out of chained و-clauses, حيث-clauses and كما-clauses, exactly the shape my doctrine calls genre A. The source is mildly corrupt in two places (السورحيثية split across tokens 140-141, and a headless خلال-adverbial at 323).
law: Genre A law applies without exception here: the annotators segment on information chunks of roughly one finite predication each, and in this genre a paragraph is a CHAIN of connective-opened links where every link is its own unit. Operative rules for this document: (1) A1 و + a new finite predication = CUT, non-negotiably; و before a bare noun or adjective (وأكبر, وماري, والبيزنطيين والمماليك والأيوبيين, ووثائق, وأبو عبيدة, سياسية واقتصادية, البيزنطية والبدوية, الأموية والدولة العباسية) = NO CUT. (2) A3 حيث = CUT, six times. (3) كما = CUT. (4) بينما = CUT. (5) A4 إلا أن = CUT. (6) ولكن = CUT. (7) A2 a fronted date or place adjunct does not protect the following و: وبعد انحسار… and وفي بعض أجزاء القلعة… each open a unit. (8) A6 asyndetic descriptive continuation = CUT when the next stretch has its own subject and predicate (تعتبر, يعود استخدام, تقع, حاليا تم العثور, لا يعرف, قيل). (9) M2/H2 every heading line is its own unit; the token before each <NL> and the final token always end a unit and an <NL> never carries one. (10) Tight subordinators never open a unit: الذي, والتي, لأن, حتى, بعد أن, عقب, بما في ذلك, أن-complements.
reasoning: Genre first, per checklist item 1. The <NL> skeleton with one-line headings plus long connective-chained history paragraphs is unambiguous genre A, so my default at every و and every ف is CUT and I must justify each non-cut (my batch-1 error profile was 7 misses per 1 false cut). WORD-LEVEL TRAP AT 140-141: token 141 is حيثية, which looks like the connective حيث but is the tail of the garbled compound الدولة السورحيثية (the Syro-Hittite state) split into السور + حيثية. I do not cut at 140; the actual boundary is at 136, before the temporal frame وبعد انحسار…. THE SIX حيث SITES: @28 (حيث احتلتها, own subject العديد من الحضارات, 14 tokens) and @275 (حيث قال الإمبراطور جوليان) and @309 (حيث أنها ضمت إلى بيزنطة) are full new predications with overt subjects, marked hi. @163 (حيث سيطرت الإمبراطورية البابلية الحديثة عليها) yields only a 6-token unit and @462 (حيث ارتقت فيما بعد) only 8, so med; @235 (حيث المنطقة الجنوبية من حلب) is verbless, but the unit that would swallow it already spends its budget on ويظهر + يصل, so 0c forces the boundary — med. THE HARDEST SITE, @169 وتلاهم الفرس: it sits exactly 6 tokens after the حيث cut at 163, right at the edge of two brakes. 0b absorbs a stranded fragment only at 5 words or fewer, and B8 says that when two candidate boundaries are 5 words apart the annotator takes the earlier and skips the later. Both brakes fire at 5, and this gap is 6, so neither narrowly applies; وتلاهم carries a finite verb, an overt subject الفرس and its own date range, which is a textbook A1 conjunct. I cut, but honestly at med — this is the one place a brake could beat A1. @322 IS DECIDED BY SEMANTICS, NOT BY A CONNECTIVE: the preceding clause ends في عام 395 م (the partition of the Roman Empire) and the next stretch is خلال الصدامات مع كسرى الثاني… في القرن السابع ميلادي. A 7th-century Sasanian clash cannot be an adjunct of a 395 AD annexation, so this fronted adverbial belongs to a new sentence whose main clause (ذكر بأن سكان حلب لجؤوا إلى القلعة) lies across the <NL> at 335. The <NL> already forces a boundary at 334, so the fronted frame must open its unit at 323 — hi. @117 كما أشير إليه is tightly anaphoric (إليه points back at the date) and closes a 28-token lead clause, so it is the weakest كما here, but the connective table has no recorded exception; cut at med. @439 إلا أن follows a 10-token unit, well clear of the B8 5-word yield window, so A4 stands; still med because the original almost certainly had only a comma there and this connective is my least-tested. @483 ولكن نقل إلى القلعة continues the same topic (the Hamdanid palace), which argues for absorption, but the unit 471-483 already holds قام plus the relative يمر, so the budget is spent and 11 further tokens is far above the short-tail threshold — cut at med. NON-CUTS I ACTIVELY DEFEND: بما في ذلك الإغريق والبيزنطيين والمماليك والأيوبيين is listed in H1 as a cataphoric announcer, but H1 is the constitutional-genre colon rule where the items sit on their own lines as full clauses; here it is four bare proper nouns riding inside one running-prose clause, which is J5 and H5 territory, so no cut at 38 and none inside 39-42. ما بين 539 333 قبل الميلاد is a date range with the dash stripped, not the standalone stray numeral of A5, so it stays inline. المسجد الكبير ومسجد إبراهيم is an appositive bare-NP pair, no cut. The main clauses after fronted بعد-frames (@188 حكمها, @268 نال) are the predicates of those frames, not new units. Long single-predication stretches (90-117, 390-414, 254-275) stay whole because nothing opens a second predication in them — length alone is never a reason to cut. RESULT: 43 units over 509 non-<NL> tokens, mean about 11.8 tokens per unit, which matches the density genre A showed in batch 1.
